$what: Provenance of ojz_act1.regions.json — the AEON HALF OF THE SHARED GOLDEN, document side. It is one act's regions document in the contract shape aurora-regions.schema.json describes, published by aeon precisely so both repos can flatten it and compare. test/formats/regions-seam.test.ts parses these bytes with Aurora's own parseRegionsDocument and flattens them, and asserts the result reproduces the rows in ojz_act1.rows.json beside it.
$why_vendored_and_not_read_at_a_revision: The same answer regions-vectors.provenance.json gives: read through `git show` AT TEST TIME the golden would vanish on a machine with no aeon beside it, and a seam test that skips when it cannot find its fixture is a seam that certifies by being absent. Vendored bytes run from a lone clone; the currency row in test/formats/aeon-fixture-currency.test.ts is what pays for the staleness. The extraction was still through git OBJECTS at a named revision, never through the sibling working tree — aeon's session was mid-parcel on the day this was vendored, so its working tree held uncommitted edits.
$why_this_document_is_the_one_worth_havi: It is not a shape sample. Its region `night` straddles the section line at x = 4096 with NEITHER edge on a multiple of the 2048 section size (x 3400..4799 exclusive-form x = 3400, w = 1400), and the two regions whose spans are its complement, `sec1` (w = 1352) and `sec2` (w = 1344), are off the grid because of it. A document whose regions all sat on the section grid could not tell a correct flattener from one that quietly snapped to sections. DO NOT TIDY IT: a re-vendor that lands a grid-aligned document keeps every row in the seam test green and silently stops exercising the thing the fixture exists for. The rows file's own `_provenance.night_is_the_point` says the same in aeon's words, and regions-seam.test.ts asserts the straddle as a property of the fixture so the loss would go red.
